entities.title: The living river
entities.description: A river connects geology, soil, plants and human life. Information becomes useful when it remains connected to a place, a question and the conditions under which it was gathered. Change the bounded terrain brush below to run a real production operation and inspect its output.

entities.title: The forest canopy
entities.description: A tree is part of biological, ecological, cultural and informational relationships. Switch the relationship lens to see how these connections cross the landscape. The world is an authored model; the linked biology, geometry and knowledge demonstrations expose their own inputs and scope.

entities.title: The commons
entities.description: Sharing knowledge should support people and their purposes. Try a synthetic community request below. The actual QualiaDB deontic evaluator processes the authored norms, and the local host returns the summary only when the selected norm permits it. Individual records are never included in the response.

entities.title: The atelier
entities.description: A sound, a model or a written work carries human intention. Synth connects a production recipe to its output, so a creator can inspect, repeat and share the work. Generate a tone, listen deliberately, then inspect the source and package.

entities.title: The field station
entities.description: How can we inspect information about the physical world? Change the amplitude of a synthetic emitter, compile an electromagnetic field, and inspect its magnitude preview. The current preview is greyscale. This is a model estimate, not a sensor measurement or a complete Maxwell solver.

entities.title: The living body
entities.description: Understanding a living body requires relationships across scale, purpose, evidence and uncertainty. The garden helix is a spatial invitation into the existing anatomy and biological demonstrations, not a biological dataset in itself.

entities.title: The field studio
entities.description: A gold 2012–13 Volkswagen Passat wagon with a streamlined charcoal roof box, a 1980 Jayco wind-up camper, two three-panel solar arrays and one two-panel array on the ground, and a Starlink Mini on the camper roof. This campsite reflects the circumstances in which this ecosystem has been developed: living, working, making and staying connected. The vehicle and camper are authored interpretations of the described models.
